newsitem.title: USA: NYC mayor supports idea of curbing tobacco ads.
newsitem.headline: NYC mayor supports idea of curbing tobacco ads.

text.p: New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani on Tuesday said he backed the City Council's idea of banning tobacco advertisements near schools.

"The mayor is supportive of the concept," said a statement released by Colleen Roche, a spokeswoman for Giuliani. She said the mayor and Council Speaker Peter Vallone had discussed the proposal, but noted there were some outstanding concerns.
"Speaker Vallone has raised some issues, however, about the scope of the bill. The mayor is interested in what the debate and the discussion in the City Council produces," the statement said.
A spokesman for the mayor was not immediately able to clarify the statement.

Earlier the council said it planned to unveil on Wednesday a bill that would restrict advertising and promotion of tobacco products within 1,000 feet of schools and other places where children gather.

A spokeswoman for Vallone, Rica Rinzler, said the council did not foresee problems with potential legal challenges. "One of the reasons the bill took so long to draft was to be sure it was constitutional and could be enforced. We are now comfortable with the bill," she said.
New York was one of the first U.S. cities to restrict smoking in restaurants, workplaces and other public areas.
